selection: Three developer-selected papers from previously retrieved Europe PMC records. Curated demonstration, not an autonomous or exhaustive literature search.

items.quote: Pooled analysis revealed no significant association between remdesivir use and CAEs (RR=0.84, 95% CI: 0.68 to 1.04, p=0.118).
items.claim: A meta-analysis did not detect an overall association between remdesivir and cardiac adverse events.
items.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
items.relevance: Overall cardiac safety context; this excerpt does not resolve human sex-specific risk.
limitations: An overall null association does not establish safety equivalence between women and men.
Included trials may overlap the input trial; do not count these as independent replications.

source.title: Cardiac adverse events associated with remdesivir in COVID-19 patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

items.quote: The study found no clinically relevant QTc prolongation from remdesivir at a supratherapeutic dose (ΔΔQTcF < 10 ms).
items.claim: A healthy-participant study reported no clinically relevant QTc prolongation at its studied single supratherapeutic dose.
items.study_design: Controlled single-dose QT study in healthy participants
items.relevance: Human cardiac repolarization context; population, dose and endpoint differ from hospitalized COVID-19 safety.
limitations: No sex-stratified risk estimate is established by the selected excerpt.
QTc is one endpoint; this result cannot establish absence of all cardiac adverse effects.

source.title: Thorough QT/QTc Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effect of Remdesivir on Cardiac Repolarization in Healthy Participants.

items.quote: Male guinea pigs were more susceptible to electrophysiological instability and mitochondrial dysfunction.
items.claim: A guinea-pig experiment reported greater male susceptibility to electrophysiological instability and mitochondrial dysfunction.
items.study_design: Preclinical experiment in male and female guinea pigs
items.relevance: Sex-dependent mechanistic hypothesis to investigate; this is animal evidence, not a finding of increased risk in women.
limitations: Animal findings cannot be treated as observed human clinical risk.
Species, route and exposure differences require investigation before clinical interpretation.

source.title: Electrophysiological and Molecular Features of Remdesivir-Induced Cardiac Toxicity in Male and Female Guinea Pigs.
